skill.name: codebase-design
skill.description: Design deep modules with small interfaces, clear seams, concentrated behavior, and practical testing strategies.
skill.summary: Evaluate and improve module depth, interface design, seam placement, dependency handling, and testability.
skill.author: mattpocock

content.value_statement: Shallow modules spread complexity across callers and make tests depend on implementation details. This skill evaluates interfaces, seams, dependencies, and alternatives to improve module depth.
actual_capabilities: Defines consistent terms for modules, interfaces, seams, adapters, depth, leverage, and locality.
Distinguishes deep modules from shallow pass-through abstractions.
Evaluates interfaces for surface area, hidden complexity, and caller leverage.
Classifies dependencies and recommends suitable testing adapters.
Generates and compares several distinct interface designs.
Recommends tests based on observable behavior through the module interface.
limitations: It provides design guidance, not automated code modification or validation.
It requires codebase context to assess coupling, dependencies, and existing interfaces accurately.
Its recommendations still require project-specific performance and operational review.
Parallel interface exploration depends on an environment that supports sub-agents.

use_cases.title: Refactor Shallow Modules
use_cases.description: Identify pass-through abstractions and consolidate behavior behind a smaller interface.
use_cases.target_user: Software engineers maintaining a growing codebase

use_cases.title: Review Architecture Changes
use_cases.description: Assess seam placement, dependency categories, and interface complexity before approving a redesign.

use_cases.title: Improve Test Boundaries
use_cases.description: Design interfaces that support observable tests without exposing internal implementation details.
use_cases.target_user: Test engineers and developers improving test suites

prompt_templates.title: Explain Module Depth
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain whether this module is deep or shallow, using its interface and hidden behavior as evidence.
prompt_templates.scenario: Learn the core vocabulary with one module.

prompt_templates.title: Assess an Interface
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this interface for unnecessary methods, complex parameters, hidden invariants, error modes, and opportunities to increase caller leverage.
prompt_templates.scenario: Evaluate a proposed or existing interface.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Deepening Refactor
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these related modules, classify their dependencies, propose a deeper replacement, and define tests through its external interface.
prompt_templates.scenario: Consolidate a cluster of shallow modules.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Alternative Designs
prompt_templates.prompt: Create four radically different interfaces, then compare depth, locality, seam placement, dependency strategy, and trade-offs before recommending one design.

output_examples.input: Review an order workflow with separate validation, pricing, payment, and persistence wrappers.
output: The wrappers are shallow because callers still coordinate ordering, errors, and shared state.
A deeper order-processing module can own the workflow behind one operation.
Inject payment and persistence adapters, then test observable outcomes through the new interface.

output_examples.input: Compare two interfaces for sending customer notifications.
output: The command-oriented interface offers higher leverage for common notification workflows.
The transport-oriented interface exposes retry, routing, and formatting decisions to every caller.
Prefer the command-oriented design unless callers genuinely require transport control.

output_examples.input: Decide how to test a module that calls an owned internal service.
output_examples.output: Define a port at the internal service seam, use a production transport adapter, and provide an in-memory adapter for module tests.

best_practices: Provide representative callers, current interfaces, and dependency details before requesting a design review.
Compare alternatives using depth, locality, seam placement, and observable test behavior.
Validate the recommended interface against real error modes, invariants, performance needs, and migration constraints.
anti_patterns: Do not add an interface when only one implementation exists and no variation is required.
Do not expose internal seams solely to make implementation-level tests easier.
Do not measure module depth by implementation size or line counts.

faq.question: What is a deep module?
faq.answer: A deep module provides substantial behavior through a small interface that callers can learn and test easily.

faq.question: What does interface mean here?
faq.answer: It includes methods, parameters, invariants, ordering constraints, errors, configuration, and performance facts callers must understand.

faq.question: When should I introduce a seam?
faq.answer: Introduce a seam when behavior genuinely varies across adapters, usually between production and testing or between distinct implementations.

faq.question: How does this skill improve testing?
faq.answer: It treats the external interface as the test surface and favors observable outcomes over internal state.

faq.question: Can it redesign an entire codebase?
faq.answer: It can guide focused module redesigns, but broad changes require staged analysis and project-specific validation.

faq.question: Does it modify source code automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides analysis, interface proposals, testing strategies, and recommendations for an implementation workflow.
